## Repository Purpose

You are helping maintain the `apt-repository` project in the `robertsinfosec` GitHub organization. This repository contains the source code and configuration that builds a Debian/Ubuntu compatible APT repository and a documentation site, both served from `https://apt.robertsinfosec.com`. It is a source repository that follows GitHub conventions, with documentation under `docs/`, implementation and build code under `src/`, and generated artifacts under `dist/`.

## Structural Conventions

Always follow these structural conventions when creating or modifying files:

- Place human oriented project documentation under `docs/`, not in the repository root and not mixed with build outputs.
- Place implementation code, build scripts, and configuration for the APT repository and docs site under `src/`. For example, APT related configuration and scripts live under `src/apt/`, and documentation site source lives under `src/docs-site/`.
- Treat `dist/` as a build artifact directory that is generated by scripts under `src/`. Do not place hand-authored source files directly into `dist/` and do not assume `dist/` contains stable inputs for development.

## APT Repository and Docs Layout

The build process will generate an APT repository layout under `dist/` that is consumed by `apt` and a static documentation site under `dist/docs/` for browser users. The APT layout must include `dist/dists/` and `dist/pool/` following Debian conventions, and the docs layout must include static HTML pages, assets, and supporting files such as `dist/index.html`, `dist/robots.txt`, and `dist/sitemap.xml`. Suggestions that move or route `dists/` or `pool/` through client side routing logic should be avoided; they are part of the deployed artifact tree, not part of the source.

When generating scripts or configuration for tools such as `reprepro`, assume that configuration files such as `distributions` and `options` live under `src/apt/conf/`, and that build scripts live under `src/apt/scripts/`. Those scripts should take `.deb` artifacts as inputs and produce or refresh `dist/dists/` and `dist/pool/` without relying on hand editing. The documentation site source under `src/docs-site/` should build into `dist/docs/`, using static site generation so that HTML content is fully present in the deployed files.

## Documentation Style

When generating markdown in this repository, use the following style guidelines:

- Assume that a top-level `#` heading may be added elsewhere, so start main headings at `##`.
- After each heading, include a descriptive paragraph of at least three to five sentences explaining the section’s purpose and context.
- Do not use bold text alone as a substitute for headings. When you need a new section, use real markdown headings (`##`, `###`, and so on).
- When creating lists, begin each item with a short **bold summary phrase** followed by one or more sentences with further explanation.

These rules apply especially to files under `docs/`, but they are also recommended for markdown files under `src/` when documenting scripts, configuration, or build behavior.

## CI and Build Expectations

When proposing or modifying CI configuration under `.github/workflows/`, assume that the main job of CI is to build the `dist/` tree. CI should, at a minimum, be able to build the APT repository structure under `dist/dists/` and `dist/pool/` from `.deb` inputs, build the static documentation site from `src/docs-site/` into `dist/docs/`, and generate or update `dist/robots.txt` and `dist/sitemap.xml`. CI may also sign APT metadata using GPG keys configured in the CI environment. Suggestions should avoid hard-coding single package names where possible and instead operate generically on provided `.deb` files.

Local developer workflows inside the dev container should mirror CI where possible. Scripts under `src/apt/scripts/` or similar helpers should be able to build an APT repository into `dist/` using a small set of `.deb` files for testing, such as the `compose-upgrade` package. When generating these scripts, include clear comments describing their inputs, outputs, and any assumptions about directory structure.

## Initial Package and Examples

The first supported package is `compose-upgrade`, a Bash based helper for robust Docker Compose upgrades. When generating examples in documentation or scripts, you may use `compose-upgrade` as the reference package name. For example, you can show how a `.deb` for `compose-upgrade` would be placed under `dist/pool/` and how the documentation under `dist/docs/` would describe installing it via `apt`. Avoid baking `compose-upgrade` directly into generic infrastructure scripts unless there is a clear reason to do so; instead, treat it as a sample package that demonstrates the repository’s capabilities.
